strengths: Well-motivated problem combining multimodal learning, cross-domain generalization, and generative forecasting in a unified framework
Strong and consistent experimental results achieving SOTA across three benchmarks (TimeMMD, TSFM-Bench, ProbTS) with comprehensive baseline comparisons (18 models)
Comprehensive system design handling multiple scenarios: multimodal/unimodal, zero-shot/few-shot, deterministic/probabilistic forecasting
Thorough experimental evaluation with extensive appendices including detailed hyperparameters, full results, efficiency analysis, and ablation studies

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components (token distillation, cross-attention, modality-guided fusion, flow matching) are standard techniques combined in a relatively straightforward manner without fundamental innovation

Critical reliance on synthetic text descriptions generated by GPT4 undermines multimodal claims; no analysis of how real human-written descriptions would differ or ablation on text description quality

Insufficient analysis of modality contributions: Missing ablations on per-modality importance, performance with missing modalities, and sensitivity to modality quality; Table 4 only removes entire modules
Ad-hoc image encoding scheme (FFT→reshape→repeat→resize) lacks justification; why this specific transformation is optimal and how it compares to alternatives is unexplored

Substantial computational cost (418.6M parameters, 30 days training on 8 A800s, 83.5ms inference) with unclear justification of whether performance gains warrant the expense; 3× larger than some efficient baselines

Weak theoretical justification for design choices: modality-guided attention via Corr matrix multiplication, prototype-based flow matching initialization, and specific fusion strategies lack principled foundations
Potential data leakage risk: >1 billion pretraining points with overlapping domains (weather, energy, health, economy) with test sets; 'strict exclusion' claim difficult to verify

Limited depth of ablation studies: Variant removal is coarse-grained; missing component-wise analysis, sensitivity to prototype bank size (M=1000 appears arbitrary), and ablation on which prototype bases matter

Generalization claims somewhat overstated: Evaluation is primarily on related domains; true out-of-distribution generalization and few-shot improvements suggest model needs fine-tuning despite pretraining
Writing quality issues including multiple typos ('merticulously', 'corrsponding', 'capablities') suggesting insufficient manuscript preparation

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks (TimeMMD, TSFM-Bench, ProbTS) with consistent improvements over 18+ baselines
Addresses both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting with practical handling of missing modalities
Strong empirical results with notable MSE reductions (27% vs. Sundial, 12.8% vs. GPT4MTS)
Extensive experimental documentation with detailed hyperparameters and full result tables
Well-motivated problem of combining multimodal information for cross-domain time series forecasting
weaknesses: Fundamental methodological flaw: Core multimodal data relies on GPT-4-generated synthetic text descriptions rather than real domain knowledge, directly contradicting stated motivation about leveraging domain-specific information; no validation of description quality or ablation vs. human annotations

Limited technical novelty: Modality-Guided Self-Attention is straightforward cross-attention; endogenous image generation is from prior work (Chen et al. 2024a); token distillation and prototype banks use standard techniques; Flow Matching novelty is primarily initialization choice

Unfair experimental comparison: Aurora trained on multimodal corpus compared against zero-shot unimodal foundation models without controlling for data access; no ablation of Aurora (multimodal) vs. Aurora (unimodal-only) on identical pretraining data; domain overlap in benchmark datasets despite exclusivity claims

Insufficient technical justification: Equation 14 (Corr = VAttn·W·TAttn^T) appears ad-hoc without principled motivation; Prototype Retriever lacks architectural detail; no empirical validation that learned prototypes capture periodicity/trend; ablations only confirm components work, not why

Lack of interpretability and analysis: No attention visualizations of modality-guided learning; missing modality contribution analysis; no case studies of failures; no sensitivity to description quality, Prototype Bank size, or robustness to varying modality availability

Reproducibility barriers: Requires 8 × A800 GPUs for 30 days (~$50k+ compute), no code release mentioned, corpus construction methodology vague, hyperparameter selection undocumented, GPT-4 API costs not discussed

Writing quality issues: Multiple consistent typos ('merticulously' ×3, 'corrsponding', 'probabilstic', 'inituitively'); grammatical inconsistencies; Figure 2 overly complex; suggests insufficient proofreading for top-tier submission

Evaluation methodology concerns: No confidence intervals or statistical significance testing; efficiency analysis (Table 8) limited to single dataset; dataset selection process unclear; few-shot comparisons use asymmetric experimental setups

Synthetic data construction: No validation that GPT-4 descriptions capture meaningful domain information; no human evaluation of description quality; no study of performance degradation with description quality; undermines claims about utilizing real domain knowledge

Missing critical analyses: No comparison of multimodal vs. unimodal model on same pretraining data; incomplete comparison with concurrent multimodal approaches; lacks visualization of learned prototypes; no analysis of which modalities provide complementary information
